Sanka Srirama Chandra Murthy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh

entities.text: Sanka Srirama Chandra Murthy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5746 Of 2019
Order:

Petitioners/A.1 to A.3 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.127 of 2019 of Ponnur Town P.S., Guntur District, which was registered against them for the offences under Sections 328, 272, 273, 188, 420, 120B IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act, 2006').
2.

The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 07.09.2019 at about 4.00 p.m., when the complainant along with his staff visited Edga of Ponnur Town, they found one unknown person with tobacco products, on that the Police stopped the person and on enquiry, he revealed that he has purchased the tobacco products from 2nd petitioner/A.2, the Police seized the same under the cover of mediator's report, arrested A.1 and A.2 and on the basis of the confession of A.2, the 3rd petitioner was also added as accused No.3, and registered the same as a case in Crime No.127 of 2019 for the offences stated supra.
3.

Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto filed on the report of the Inspector of Police of Ponnur Town Police Station.
Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners under Sections 328, 272, 273, 188, 420, 120B Sanka Srirama Chandra Murthy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 20 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163673280/
1 IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
